methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specifications were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the truth table entries and the overall functional description were separated. For the generated specifications, each statement describing a behavior, logic gate implementation, or signal dependency was treated as an atomic unit.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Q changes on the positive edge of clk
When J=0 and K=0, Q retains its previous value (Qold)
When J=0 and K=1, Q resets to 0
When J=1 and K=0, Q sets to 1
When J=1 and K=1, Q toggles to the complement of its previous value (~Qold)
Module has inputs clk, j, k and output Q
Q is updated based on J and K
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, j, k and output Q
clk input is for sequential logic
Combinational logic implements JK flip-flop's next-state logic
Truth table: J=0, K=0, Q(t+1) = Qold
Truth table: J=0, K=1, Q(t+1) = 0
Truth table: J=1, K=0, Q(t+1) = 1
Truth table: J=1, K=1, Q(t+1) = ~Qold
Q(t+1) = J & !Qold | !K & Qold
Case 1: j = 0, k = 0: Q retains its previous value (Qold)
Case 2: j = 0, k = 1: Q is reset to 0
Case 3: j = 1, k = 0: Q is set to 1
Case 4: j = 1, k = 1: Q toggles its value (inverts Qold)
Combinational logic can be implemented using AND, OR, NOT, and XOR gates
